subject: Cumtom probability distribution random number generator

messages.author: df2011c04ce6269d
messages.subject: Cumtom probability distribution random number generator
parts:
I wrote a skellam_log distribution and skellam_rng sampler in functions block. But my skellam_rng solution slows down the whole proces.
At the same time, I can not sample it in model block because Stan doesn't support discrete parameters.
What's the better approach? Can I call Stan's HMC for custom probability distribution in functions block?

We might be better able to help if you share the code.
> At the same time, I can not sample it in model block because Stan doesn't support discrete parameters.
There's no way to have discrete parameters in Stan.
> What's the better approach? Can I call Stan's HMC for custom probability distribution in functions block?

I'm not sure I understand what you're asking. Yes, you
can define a function and use it in the Stan program.
See the manual chapter on function definitions for how to define
a function you can use with sampling notation (just has to end
in _log).

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Cumtom probability distribution random number generator
parts:
That's the easy way around for a compound distribution:

int skellam_rng(real mu1, real mu2) {
return poisson_rng(mu1) - poisson_rng(mu2);
}

I just followed the definition here:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skellam_distribution

Neat model, by the way --- it even calculates WAIC.

I didn't understand why you needed to use the Skellam
here rather than just modeling homeScore and
awayScore directly. Do you know if the GLM for expected
home and away scoring are enough to deal with overdispersion
in the data?

- Bob

On Wednesday, January 28, 2015 at 7:25:29 AM UTC+8, Bob Carpenter wrote:
That's the easy way around for a compound distribution:
 
  int skellam_rng(real mu1, real mu2) {
    return poisson_rng(mu1) - poisson_rng(mu2);
  }
 
I just followed the definition here:

  http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skellam_distribution
I panned predictive inference by using scipy's skellam_log in python but I still expect rng of custom probability exists in Stan by some way.

Neat model, by the way --- it even calculates WAIC.

I didn't understand why you needed to use the Skellam
here rather than just modeling homeScore and
awayScore directly.  Do you know if the GLM for expected
home and away scoring are enough to deal with overdispersion
in the data?
I originally refered to Bivariate Poisson model but I figure out Skellam reduces assumptions from Bivariate Poisson and covers more situations with less parameters.

- Bob
